abstract.t:
In scaled Resource Reservation Protocol - Traffic Engineering (RSVP- TE) networks, a single network resource event (such as a link failure or bandwidth reduction) can trigger a storm of PathErr messages, one for each affected Label Switched Path (LSP). This document introduces RSVP Resource Notifications, a mechanism that reduces the number of per-LSP error messages by sending summarized per-source resource-level notifications in a new RSVP message, ResourceNotify. This reduces the control-plane message load from O(LSPs) to O(sources), significantly improving convergence in networks with a large number of RSVP-TE LSPs.
The mechanism applies to LSPs whose source is reachable by the transit node within the same domain, and uses a Resource Notification Request Object carried in PATH messages. Two types of resource notifications are defined in this document: Resource Unavailable (for link failures) and Resource Degraded (for bandwidth reduction events).
